episode.title: Cap shell-output truncation by the remaining model context budget
episode.before: At parent commit 4f91037af49556763fe3e5bd15a71016a5b69e88, Config.getTruncateToolOutputThreshold() returned only the configured threshold. The shell-tool scheduler already used that getter when deciding how many output characters to retain, so the effective threshold did not shrink when the preceding prompt had consumed most of the model's context window.
episode.after: At commit b416508ef1c64db6cdac2f185afa579368c353cf, Config.getTruncateToolOutputThreshold() returns the smaller of the configured threshold and four times the model token limit minus the latest prompt token count. Thus, when shell-output truncation is enabled, the existing scheduler receives a context-aware character threshold while retaining a lower default or custom configured cap.
episode.diff: The change imports the model token-limit lookup and UI telemetry service into the configuration module, replaces the fixed threshold getter with Math.min(4 * (tokenLimit(model) - lastPromptTokenCount), configuredThreshold), and adds focused tests for a remaining-context cap below the default, preservation of the default when it is lower, and both branches with a custom configured threshold. The scheduler call site and truncation mechanism are unchanged.

evidence_units.claim: Commit b416508ef1c64db6cdac2f185afa579368c353cf is the implementation-bearing resolution for PR/issue 8379, has parent 4f91037af49556763fe3e5bd15a71016a5b69e88, and changes only config.ts and config.test.ts.
In the parent state, getTruncateToolOutputThreshold() returned this.truncateToolOutputThreshold without consulting model capacity or prompt usage.

The resolved state computes the returned threshold as Math.min(4 * (tokenLimit(this.model) - uiTelemetryService.getLastPromptTokenCount()), this.truncateToolOutputThreshold), with the comment that one token is estimated as four characters.

The configured truncation threshold remains the caller-provided value when present, otherwise DEFAULT_TRUNCATE_TOOL_OUTPUT_THRESHOLD; the change modifies the getter rather than this initialization contract.
evidence_units.source: git show b416508ef1c64db6cdac2f185afa579368c353cf:packages/core/src/config/config.ts, constructor initialization of truncateToolOutputThreshold

evidence_units.claim: The token-limit helper maps a model identifier to its context-token capacity and falls back to DEFAULT_TOKEN_LIMIT for unlisted models.
The telemetry service exposes getLastPromptTokenCount(), returning its stored latest-prompt token count, which starts at zero and can be reset to zero.
evidence_units.source: git show b416508ef1c64db6cdac2f185afa579368c353cf:packages/core/src/telemetry/uiTelemetry.ts, UiTelemetryService state and accessors

evidence_units.claim: For successful string output from the shell tool, the scheduler checks that truncation is enabled and that threshold and line limits are positive, then passes getTruncateToolOutputThreshold() to truncateAndSaveToFile; this call site is unchanged from the parent.
evidence_units.source: git show b416508ef1c64db6cdac2f185afa579368c353cf:packages/core/src/core/coreToolScheduler.ts and git show 4f91037af49556763fe3e5bd15a71016a5b69e88:packages/core/src/core/coreToolScheduler.ts, shell-output handling

evidence_units.claim: A focused test sets a 32,000-token model limit and a 1,000-token prompt count and expects a 124,000-character threshold, proving that a smaller estimated remaining-context budget overrides the 4,000,000-character default.
evidence_units.source: git show b416508ef1c64db6cdac2f185afa579368c353cf:packages/core/src/config/config.test.ts, getTruncateToolOutputThreshold test 'should return the calculated threshold when it is smaller than the default'

evidence_units.claim: A focused test sets a calculated remaining-context estimate of 6,000,000 characters and expects the 4,000,000-character default, proving the existing configured ceiling is preserved when lower.
evidence_units.source: git show b416508ef1c64db6cdac2f185afa579368c353cf:packages/core/src/config/config.test.ts, getTruncateToolOutputThreshold test 'should return the default threshold when the calculated value is larger'

evidence_units.claim: A custom-threshold test expects 24,000 when remaining capacity is below a 50,000-character custom cap and expects 50,000 when the custom cap is below remaining capacity.
evidence_units.source: git show b416508ef1c64db6cdac2f185afa579368c353cf:packages/core/src/config/config.test.ts, getTruncateToolOutputThreshold test 'should use a custom truncateToolOutputThreshold if provided'

evidence_units.claim: The core package defines its unit-test command as vitest run, but the inspected evidence does not contain a recorded execution result for the pinned commit.

candidate_atomics.name: cap-output-threshold-by-remaining-context
candidate_atomics.title: Cap retained tool output by the remaining context window
candidate_atomics.description: Derive the output-character threshold from both the configured ceiling and an estimate of remaining model capacity, selecting the smaller value before the existing truncation call site consumes it.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent a configured shell-output allowance from exceeding the estimated context capacity left after the latest prompt while preserving stricter configured limits.
semantic_action.pre_state: The output-budget provider returns a static configured character threshold even though model context capacity and the latest prompt token count are available.
semantic_action.post_state: The provided character threshold is the minimum of the configured ceiling and the estimated remaining token capacity converted at four characters per token.
semantic_action.validation: Mock the model token limit and latest prompt usage, then assert both minimum-selection branches for default and custom configured ceilings.

candidate_atomics.name: verify-context-aware-threshold-branches
candidate_atomics.title: Verify context and configuration threshold precedence
candidate_atomics.description: Exercise the threshold policy with controlled capacity and usage values to prove that remaining context wins when smaller and the configured ceiling wins otherwise, including custom configuration.

semantic_action.intent: Establish a regression oracle for the precedence between dynamic remaining capacity and the pre-existing configured threshold.
semantic_action.pre_state: The threshold policy lacks focused examples demonstrating which bound wins under default and custom configurations.
semantic_action.post_state: Tests encode expected results for a smaller remaining-context bound, a smaller default bound, and both precedence branches for a custom bound.
semantic_action.validation: Run the core configuration unit tests and require the expected thresholds 124000, 4000000, 24000, and 50000 for the corresponding mocked inputs.

candidate_workflows.name: make-tool-output-budget-context-aware
candidate_workflows.title: Bound tool output by both configured limits and remaining context
candidate_workflows.description: Adapt an existing tool-output truncation path so its budget responds to current context consumption without replacing its configured safety ceiling or its downstream truncation mechanism.

workflow_graph.goal: Ensure retained shell output cannot exceed either the configured character ceiling or the estimated space remaining in the active model context.
when_to_use: A tool-output truncation path already accepts a character threshold, but that threshold is static while prompt usage varies.
The runtime can identify the active model's token capacity and observe the latest prompt token count.
Oversized tool output can consume context needed for the next model request.
anti_goals: Do not replace or raise a stricter default or user-supplied truncation ceiling.
Do not rewrite the downstream truncation, file-spill, line-retention, or telemetry behavior when the threshold provider is the missing policy boundary.
Do not apply this policy to unrelated tool results when the established call site is scoped to successful string output from the shell tool.
Do not present the four-characters-per-token estimate as exact tokenization.
not_applicable_when: No reliable model context limit or current prompt-usage measurement is available.
The consumer requires an exact tokenizer-derived byte or token bound rather than an approximate character threshold.
Tool-output truncation is disabled or the output path does not consume the threshold provider.
inputs: existing truncation consumer and its enablement guards
workflow_graph.entry_state: The scheduler already truncates eligible shell output using a configured threshold, but that threshold is independent of how much model context the latest prompt consumed.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Eligible shell output is passed to the existing truncation mechanism with the smaller of the configured ceiling and the estimated remaining-context character budget, with focused tests covering precedence branches.

steps.condition: Apply when model capacity and latest prompt usage can be read at threshold-evaluation time.
steps.validation: Inspect the threshold provider and confirm it selects Math.min of the configured ceiling and four times remaining tokens; confirm the existing scheduler consumes the getter.

steps.condition: Run after the dynamic cap is implemented.
steps.validation: The focused unit cases must prove remaining capacity wins when smaller and the default or custom configured ceiling wins when smaller.

validation_ladder: Static diff check: the fixed getter is replaced by a minimum of the dynamic remaining-context estimate and configured ceiling.
Call-site check: the guarded shell-output path still obtains the threshold through the changed provider and passes it to the existing truncation function.
Focused unit check: verify the 124000 and 4000000 default-ceiling cases.
Configuration compatibility check: verify both 24000 and 50000 custom-ceiling cases.
Package check: run the core package's vitest suite when a materialized checkout and dependencies are available.
stop_conditions: Stop if the model token limit or latest prompt token count cannot be obtained without introducing an ungrounded proxy.
Stop if changing the threshold provider would affect consumers whose budget semantics differ from the inspected shell-output call site.
Stop and repair if the dynamic calculation can exceed the configured ceiling or if custom threshold precedence fails.
Do not claim runtime validation unless the relevant test command completes successfully.
unresolved_or_deferred: The implementation can calculate zero or a negative value when reported prompt tokens meet or exceed the model limit; the scheduler's positive-threshold guard then bypasses truncation, but this boundary is not covered by the added tests.
The four-characters-per-token conversion is explicitly an estimate; no tokenizer-based accuracy validation is included.
No successful local or CI test execution result is present in the supplied evidence.

unresolved_questions: Should the remaining-context estimate be clamped to a positive value so an exhausted or over-limit prompt cannot disable the scheduler's truncation branch?
Does the latest prompt token count include all context components relevant to the next request, or only the last recorded prompt metric?
The supplied checkout has its tracked files removed from the working tree, so validation is grounded in pinned Git objects and added test code rather than a newly executed test run.
